$comment: Generated by scripts/measure-perf.mjs --write. Ceilings on measurements of this implementation, 15% over the observed run. A value above one of these is a regression to investigate, not a number to negotiate.
$gate: A metric only fails the run when `gate` is true. Timings depend on the machine; byte counts, request counts, DOM size and the eager/lazy decision the wall made are properties of the page and fail anywhere.

bytes.why: a content-length reported by the server, summed after the long scroll, so it is not a property of the host

requests.why: a count of URLs the document referenced

eagerImages.why: the `loading` attribute the wall chose per plate — the decision itself, which is what stops a 500-tile wall fetching 500 plates

loadedImages.why: a race between the viewport strategy and the network — the same wall measured 7 and 87 on consecutive runs. `eagerImages` is the decision and is gated; this is the outcome and is not

documentBytes.why: a function of how many entries the catalogue holds, so it moves when content is published rather than when code regresses; `eagerImages` and `domNodes` are the ceilings that catch a rendering regression

cls.why: depends on when a frame lands, so it moves with the host

loadMs.why: wall clock on whatever machine ran it

ttfbMs.why: server render plus, in dev, Vite module compilation

drillInMs.why: a real click and navigation; the server render dominates and the server is the host

structural: a measured route answering anything but 200
a lazy image above the fold
a video, audio, canvas, iframe, object or embed instantiated by the page
a scale wall that did not render the number of tiles it was asked for
